prompt:
Paint the COMPLETE top-down map of a very unusual fantasy SNOW VILLAGE buried in deep snowdrifts in a land of endless night, as ONE finished game map image, in rich premium modern hi-bit pixel art (the "HD pixel art" JRPG look: hand-placed crisp square pixels, hue-shifted ramps, dark warm outlines), flat classic top-down RPG map view (NOT an HD-2D diorama, no depth-of-field, no tilt-shift, no 3D render).

This is NOT an ordinary village of square log cabins, and nothing is arranged in rows or on a grid. The village lies inside huge, wind-sculpted SNOWDRIFTS; narrow trodden-snow lanes wind between the drifts like trenches and tunnels. Its heart is a round stone fire circle with a great stone hearth. Curled around the north side of that circle lies ONE enormous serpentine LONGHOUSE whose long snow-laden roof rises and falls in humps like the back of a sleeping white dragon (the village's pact with the dragon of the peak): its west end is a carved wooden DRAGON HEAD gable, and it holds four places, each with its own door in its dark tarred-log front wall: the item shop (west, lowest), the inn (next), the great hall (the middle, highest and widest hump, with a copper chimney hood), and the armourer (east); its tail sinks into a drift east of the armourer. The homes are all different: the chief's ROUND STONE TOWER-HOUSE with a conical slate roof, the fire-keeper's DOME BUILT OF CLEAR ICE BLOCKS glowing faintly, a grandmother's half-buried PIT HOUSE that is only a round snow-covered turf mound with a stovepipe and a low stone front, the hunter's LODGE of stretched hides framed by great curved MAMMOTH TUSKS, a little FISHING HUT standing on sled runners out on the frozen pond, and at the far south-east edge one cold, square, grey cut-stone building with iron shutters that looks foreign and out of place (an outsiders' office, boarded up). There is also a tall timber WATCHTOWER with a bronze bell by the north gate, a small food store on stilts, and an open lean-to sled shed.

The attached image is an exact LAYOUT GUIDE (trace over it: your painting will be laid pixel-for-pixel on top of it and checked against it, so do not shift, shrink, mirror or re-arrange anything; keep every edge within a few pixels of the guide) drawn on a 56 x 50 tile grid (each tile = 48 x 48 px of the output, output is 2688 x 2400). Every shape must sit exactly where it is in the guide at the same size: this image is used directly as the walkable game map, so positions are collision data.

Guide colour key:
- steel blue = DEEP SNOWDRIFTS (unwalkable): tall, soft, rounded, wind-carved banks of snow seen from above, with blue-violet shadows in their hollows, wind ripples, sastrugi ridges, a few buried fence posts, frozen bare shrubs and snow-laden young firs poking out. Where a darker blue band runs along the bottom edge of a drift, paint the drift's steep shadowed FRONT BANK facing the lane below (a short vertical wall of packed snow with icicles and a lip of overhanging snow). The outer border of the map is all deep drift.
- off-white = open, flat snow (walkable): smooth fresh snow with faint footprints and sled tracks, a little blown snow. Keep it FLAT.
- warm tan with dots = trodden snow LANES (walkable): packed, dirtied snow with footprints, straw and ash strewn for grip, sled runner grooves. Flat.
- grey with circles (centre) = the FIRE CIRCLE: a round, sunken plaza of old flat stones set in rings around the hearth, swept clear of snow, with carved ring patterns. Flat, no objects on it (the game places braziers, benches and a stall there).
- dark ring with orange centre = the GREAT HEARTH: a low, wide ring of big blackened stones with glowing embers in the middle, carvings of a dragon and a girl on the rim.
- cyan = the FROZEN POND (walkable ice): pale blue-green ice with cracks, trapped bubbles, and dusted snow near the shore.
- brown with vertical plank lines (top, beside the gate lane) = the watchmen's timber LOOKOUT DECK (walkable planks).
- pale lavender blocks with a dark ridge line = the LONGHOUSE ROOF: thick snow on a long humped roof with dragon-scale wooden shingles showing along the ridge and at the eaves, icicles hanging from the eaves, stovepipes and chimneys puffing; the humps flow into each other as ONE continuous curving building (also over the narrow pale blocks that join the parts). Dark brown bands under it = the tarred-log FRONT WALLS facing the viewer, with the doors and small warm windows; hang a carved sign-board beside each door.
- dark slate circle over a grey front = the chief's round stone tower-house (conical slate roof seen from above, curved grey stone front).
- cyan circle with arcs = the ice-block dome house (translucent ice blocks, a wooden door frame and a short ice-block entrance porch at the front).
- white oval with a dark dot and a small grey front = the pit house (snow-covered turf mound, stovepipe at the dot, low dry-stone front with the door).
- brown oval with ivory arcs = the hunter's hide lodge: stretched hides and furs over a frame of huge mammoth tusks (the ivory arcs), antlers, with a planked front wall.
- grey rectangle (lower right) = the outsiders' square stone office: flat grey stone roof, iron-shuttered windows, planks nailed across, no snow decoration, looking cold and unwelcome.
- small brown box on the pond with a line under it = the fishing hut on sled runners.
- brown box with an X and a gold circle (top) = the timber watchtower seen from above, with the bronze bell.
- small brown box on two legs (top right) = the food store on stilts. Brown box with a dark opening (lower left) = the open lean-to sled shed (no door).
- small BLACK rectangles = the front DOORS. Each door must be painted exactly at that spot and size (a wooden door, bottom edge on the bottom edge of the wall). The black arch in the drift south of the fire circle is a child-sized tunnel hole dug into the snow bank (a secret den). Do not add any other door or opening that looks like a door.
- small yellow squares = small windows (panes softly warm, but no glow spilling out).
Buildings and drifts must not extend outside their guide shapes.

Make everything rich, detailed, handcrafted and cohesive, like a lovingly painted JRPG town map of a snowbound northern village preparing a midwinter fire festival: garlands of dried berries and pine on the longhouse, rune-carved posts, fur hangings, snow on every ledge. Details on walkable ground must stay flat (no tall things on the walkable areas).

Pixel art rules: crisp square pixels, no blur, no anti-aliasing, no painterly brush strokes, no noise, clear clusters, hue-shifted ramps, dark warm outlines on buildings. Characters in this game are about 140 output px tall, so details should be at that scale.
Lighting: this is the ALBEDO base layer. Neutral, soft, even daylight-like light; NO night, NO cast shadows longer than a few pixels, NO lamp light pools, NO glow, NO vignette, NO fog, no falling snow.
Do NOT paint any characters, animals, lamp posts, lanterns, braziers, barrels, crates, benches, wells, market stalls, signs, sleds on the ground, chests, text, labels, grid lines or UI. Leave open ground for them.
